subject.title: [Bug]: iOS app fails to connect over Tailscale CGNAT (100.x.x.x) — wss:// required but WebSocket upgrade silently dropped

question: What should the supported iOS Tailscale remote pairing policy be for raw 100.64/10 CGNAT addresses versus MagicDNS/Tailscale Serve/TLS-pinned endpoints?
rationale: The obvious fixes point in different security directions: accepting raw tailnet plaintext improves connectivity but relaxes mobile transport policy, while secure-only onboarding requires clearer UX and live proof rather than a simple code toggle.

options.title: Keep Secure-Only Tailscale Onboarding
options.body: Require MagicDNS, Tailscale Serve/Funnel, or native TLS with a trusted fingerprint, and improve iOS diagnostics for raw 100.x inputs and unreachable Serve routes.

options.title: Approve Explicit Tailnet Plaintext
options.body: Allow raw CGNAT or `.ts.net` plaintext only behind an explicit user/operator opt-in with docs and tests that bound the trust model.

options.title: Require Native Gateway TLS First
options.body: Make direct Tailscale CGNAT support depend on a configured Gateway certificate and a reliable iOS fingerprint trust prompt before connecting.

recommendation.title: Keep Secure-Only Tailscale Onboarding
recommendation.body: Require MagicDNS, Tailscale Serve/Funnel, or native TLS with a trusted fingerprint, and improve iOS diagnostics for raw 100.x inputs and unreachable Serve routes.

likelyOwner.reason: The unresolved choice is primarily a TLS/auth security-boundary decision, and this history shows steipete carried the adjacent TLS trust, discovery hardening, and Tailscale auth policy work.
